Active Planned Care / GoalsStart DateReason
Discharge care plan24-Mar-2010History of aortic valve replacement (situation)
  • Ensure patient and/or caregiver demonstrates understanding of discharge instructions, including medication regimen, activity restrictions, wound care, and signs of complications following aortic valve replacement.
  • Patient will adhere to the prescribed medication regimen following aortic valve replacement to reduce risk of complications.
  • Patient will attend all scheduled follow-up appointments with cardiology and primary care after discharge.
  • Maintain systolic and diastolic blood pressure within target range to reduce cardiovascular risk after aortic valve replacement.
  • Maintain fasting blood glucose within individualized target range to reduce risk of complications after aortic valve replacement.
  • Patient will gradually increase physical activity as tolerated, following discharge instructions and cardiac rehabilitation recommendations.
  • Patient will work towards achieving and maintaining a healthy weight following discharge.
  • Patient will implement strategies to prevent COPD exacerbations, including medication adherence, avoidance of triggers, and prompt reporting of symptoms.
  • Patient will adhere to osteoporosis management plan to support bone health and reduce fracture risk after discharge.
  • Patient will attend regular ophthalmology follow-up for diabetic retinopathy monitoring after discharge.
  • Maintain LDL cholesterol within target range to reduce cardiovascular risk after aortic valve replacement.
  • Patient will adhere to recommended colonoscopy surveillance schedule for colon polyp monitoring after discharge.
  • Patient will implement strategies to manage hand osteoarthritis symptoms and maintain hand function after discharge.
Care plan17-Mar-2010Aortic valve stenosis (disorder)
  • Minimize dyspnea, fatigue, and other symptoms related to aortic valve stenosis to improve daily functioning and quality of life.
  • Maintain systolic blood pressure within target range to reduce cardiac workload.
  • Maintain HbA1c within individualized target to reduce cardiovascular risk.
  • Maintain LDL cholesterol below target to reduce progression of atherosclerosis.
